quarterly.period_note: Year-end (31 December 2025) position from NRB Commercial Bank's 'Annual Integrated Report 2025', taken from its own 'Five Years' Key Performance Indicators' table (printed pages 49-50, physical PDF pages 50-51), which is explicitly captioned 'Last Five years' (2021 to 2025) Balance Sheet (Solo)' / '...Profit & Loss Statement (Solo)' elsewhere in the same report. Basis is therefore explicitly SOLO, confirmed both by that caption and by the standard match-total-assets method: this table's own FY2024 column for 'Size of Balance Sheet' (230,593.06) reproduces the existing dataset's stored solo FY2024 total_assets exactly. This PDF is entirely image-based (pdftotext -layout returns 0 lines; native embedded page images are only 845x1233px at 72ppi) so all figures were read directly off the rendered table image at 300dpi with additional 2-3x crops/zooms on ambiguous cells, and cross-checked line-by-line against the existing FY2024 record for consistency (see discrepancies below). DISCREPANCIES FOUND vs the already-stored FY2024 record (FY2024 file left unchanged; both values recorded here): (1) Deposit: FY2024's own report states 183,282.14; this FY2025 report's FY2024 comparative column states 169,737.39 instead (a 13,544.75 / 7.4% reduction). Total assets (230,593.06) and gross loans (147,576.45) for FY2024 reproduce exactly across both reports, so this looks like a reclassification within liabilities (some deposit-like balance moved to another liability line) rather than a broad restatement. (2) Profit after tax: FY2024's own report states 35.88, which does not arithmetically reconcile with that same report's own profit-before-tax (44.43) minus provision for taxation (-0.34) = 44.77. This FY2025 report's FY2024 comparative column states 44.77, which DOES reconcile exactly with the same PBT/tax figures (both reports agree PBT=44.43 and tax=-0.34). This mirrors the ISLAMIBANK FY2024-capital precedent: the contemporaneous figure is arithmetically inconsistent with its own report, while the later report's comparative is internally consistent. (3) 'Operating income' definitional difference (not a value restatement): FY2024's own report's five-year table computed 'Operating income' as gross interest income + investment income + non-interest income = 12,481.25+5,548.54+1,772.77 = 19,802.56 (before deducting interest expense). This FY2025 report's table computes the same line as NET interest income + investment income + non-interest income = 187.02+5,548.54+1,772.77 = 7,508.33 for the identical FY2024 year. Every underlying component (interest income, interest expense, net interest income, investment income, non-interest income) reproduces exactly across both reports, so this is purely a change in which formula the bank's own report labels 'Operating income', not a restated transaction; total_operating_income below uses THIS report's own (net-interest-income-based) figure for FY2025, consistent with how FY2025's own table defines it. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY found within the FY2025 report's own table (not a cross-report issue): Core Capital/Tier I (11,481.23) + Supplementary Capital/Tier II (7,389.06) = 18,870.29, but the same table's own 'Regulatory Capital [Tier I + II]' row prints 18,083.74 (786.55 / 4.3% short of the sum of its own two components). Three independent figures in the same table tie out to 18,083.74 and not to 18,870.29: Capital Surplus/(Shortfall) of -2,183.36 equals 18,083.74 minus Capital Requirement of 20,267.10 exactly; CRAR of 11.15% equals 18,083.74 / RWA of 162,136.81 exactly; and the printed Tier-II Capital Ratio of 4.07% implies a Tier II capital of approximately 6,599-6,603 (RWA x 4.07%, and also exactly 18,083.74 minus the printed Tier I of 11,481.23 = 6,602.51), not the printed 7,389.06. The Tier-I ratio (7.08%) does tie to the printed Tier I capital. All three re-verified visually at 3x crop zoom - the printed digits are unambiguous. This strongly suggests the printed Tier II CAPITAL AMOUNT cell (7,389.06) is a typo in the source document; it is recorded here exactly as printed (basis 'reported'), with total_capital taken as the table's own printed total (18,083.74, consistent with its CRAR and capital-surplus rows) rather than derived by summing the two tier components as prior years' methodology would otherwise do. Asset-quality and capital trends continued to deteriorate in FY2025 despite a profit recovery: NPL rose to 17.17% (from 15.47%), CRAR fell to 11.15% (from 12.00%) and the capital shortfall widened to -2,183.36 (from -754.81); Tier-1 fell to 7.08% (from 7.64%). Profit after tax recovered to 329.83m from the FY2024 trough (35.88m per FY2024's own report / 44.77m per this report) but remains far below FY2021-2023 levels (1,739.57-2,083.94m). ldr_pct below uses the bank's own reported 'Credit Deposit Ratio' (77.71%), which does not equal a naive gross-loans/deposits calculation from this same table (162,469.79/198,424.61=81.88%) - likely a regulatory definition or averaging difference; both figures are noted here for transparency.

insights.methodology: Derived from bank_financials/NRBCBANK/quarterly/*.json (FY2013-FY2025 year-end) and ratios_timeseries.json. Every figure is a reported value from NRB Commercial Bank's own audited annual report summary tables, or an explicitly-labelled derivation. Note the basis break: FY2013-FY2019 are consolidated, FY2020-FY2025 solo (0.12% apart at FY2018; FY2025 explicitly labelled 'Solo' in its own source table). Two extraction traps were resolved arithmetically before sourcing FY2013-2024 — see sources.json. The FY2025 annual report PDF is image-based with no text layer; its figures were read directly from the rendered table image, cross-checked cell-by-cell against the existing FY2024 record (two genuine discrepancies found: Deposit and Profit after tax for FY2024, both documented without altering the existing FY2024 file), and an internal Tier I/Tier II/Regulatory Capital inconsistency within the FY2025 report's own table was found and is recorded rather than silently resolved. No figure is interpolated or estimated.

risk_signals.statement: Classified loans went from 7,756m (5.35% of the book) at end-FY2023 to 22,837m (15.47%) at end-FY2024, a 194% increase in one year, while the loan book grew only 1.7%. Profit after tax collapsed to 36m from 1,846m — a 98.1% fall — and profit before tax to 44m from 2,528m. For context the reported NPL ratio had never exceeded 5.35% in the bank's eleven prior years. This is the same FY2024 break seen at IFIC, Islami Bank and National Bank, arriving at a much smaller and younger bank.

NRBC fell into a capital shortfall of 754.81m in FY2024 against its 18,747m requirement including conservation buffer, having reported a 1,753.72m surplus a year earlier. Reported CRAR fell to 12.00% from 13.70%, and the Tier-I ratio to 7.64% from 8.80% — below the 8.5% Tier-I-plus-buffer expectation. Regulatory capital fell 2,015m in absolute terms (20,008m to 17,992m) as losses ate into Tier-I.

Provision held against classified loans rose from 3,594m to 5,042m in FY2024, a 40% increase, while classified loans themselves rose 194% to 22,837m. Coverage therefore fell from 46.3% to 22.1%, the lowest in the bank's history, leaving 17,794m of unprovided classified exposure against 13,297m of stockholder equity — 1.34 times equity. Fully providing for it would erase the bank's capital.

Net interest income collapsed to 187m in FY2024 from 3,769m in FY2023 — a 95% fall — as interest expense rose 43.3% to 12,294m while interest income was almost flat at 12,481m. The bank stayed marginally profitable only because investment income rose 80.9% to 5,549m. Expressed against the loan book the net interest margin fell from 2.60% to 0.13%.

Stockholder equity fell from 14,180m to 13,297m in FY2024, the first decline in the bank's twelve-year history — it had risen every year from 4,399m in FY2013. Because the FY2024 profit was only 36m, the fall implies distributions or reserve adjustments exceeding earnings.

Total assets compounded at 33.6% a year from FY2013 to FY2024, from 9,538m to 230,593m — a 24-fold increase in eleven years, and the fastest growth of any bank in this dataset. Loans grew from 3,717m to 147,576m over the same span. The FY2024 asset-quality break landed on a book built almost entirely in the preceding decade, and the reported NPL ratio gave little warning: it was still 5.35% the year before the jump to 15.47%.

Deposit growth fell to 4.3% in FY2024 (175,670m to 183,282m, per FY2024's own report) from 30.0% in FY2021 and 29.3% in FY2022. Combined with total asset growth of 5.8%, the balance sheet had essentially stopped expanding for the first time in the bank's history — a marked change for an institution that had compounded assets at 33.6% a year. FY2025 shows renewed growth (see fy2025_partial_recovery_with_deepening_capital_shortfall), though FY2025's own report puts FY2024 deposits at 169,737m instead, a discrepancy documented in sources.json.

NRBC's capital shortfall widened to 2,183.36m in FY2025 from 754.81m in FY2024 (2.9x), against a requirement (including conservation buffer) that itself grew to 20,267.10m from 18,747.21m. Reported CRAR fell to 11.15% from 12.00% — the second straight annual decline after an FY2023 bounce (12.44% at FY2022, 13.70% at FY2023, 12.00% at FY2024, 11.15% at FY2025) — and now sits 1.35 points below the FY2024 level and well under the ~12.5% full requirement. Tier-1 fell to 7.08% from 7.64%. This is the bank's second consecutive year of an actual (not just marginal) capital deficit.

Profit after tax recovered to 329.83m in FY2025 from FY2024's 35.88m trough (or 44.77m per FY2025's own restated comparative) — nominally an 819% increase, but the base was a near-zero crisis year and the FY2025 result itself remains 81-84% below the 1,739.57m-2,083.94m the bank earned every year from FY2021-2023. Meanwhile classified loans grew a further 22.1% to 27,890.61m, faster than the 10.1% growth in the loan book, extending the NPL ratio's unbroken climb every year since FY2020 to a new high of 17.17% (2.93% -> 4.56% -> 4.69% -> 5.35% -> 15.47% -> 17.17% across FY2020-FY2025). The book is growing again (total assets +13.6%, deposits +8.3%) but asset quality has not stabilised and capital adequacy is still deteriorating alongside it (see fy2025_capital_shortfall_widened_to_second_consecutive_year).

Newly-added Q1-Q3 2024 quarterly data (this session) shows the FY2024 collapse described elsewhere in this file was not spread evenly through the year. Profit after tax was still 335.44m in Q1, 269.79m in Q2 and 93.70m in Q3 -- a weakening trend, but nowhere near the annual-level damage. Almost the entire year's loss landed in Q4 alone: with full-year profit after tax at 44.77m (the internally-reconciling figure; 35.88m per the FY2024 report's own since-flagged inconsistent headline), Q4 alone implies a discrete loss of approximately -654m to -663m (annual minus the 698.93m Q1-Q3 sum). Net interest income shows the same pattern even more starkly: positive and growing through Q1 (825.85m), Q2 (1,046.21m) and Q3 (580.60m), before swinging to -2,265.65m in Q4 alone -- which is also why the deceptively mild full-year figure of 187.02m obscures a genuinely catastrophic single quarter rather than a year of gradually eroding margins.

Newly-added Q1-Q3 2025 quarterly data (this session) shows the profit recovery described in fy2025_partial_recovery_with_deepening_capital_shortfall is not a lending-margin story. Discrete net interest income stayed compressed all year -- 491.35m in Q1, just 47.78m in Q2, and 58.97m in Q3, versus 825.85m / 1,046.21m / 580.60m in the equivalent 2024 quarters -- while investment income grew every quarter (1,409.51m, then 1,487.80m, then 1,873.89m). Profit after tax was correspondingly weak and backloaded: 51.68m in Q1, falling further to 10.34m in Q2, only partially recovering to 66.63m in Q3. The three quarters combined (128.65m) are barely a third of the full-year 329.83m, implying a discrete Q4 2025 profit of approximately 201.18m -- 61% of the entire year's profit landing in a single quarter.

Newly-added Q1-Q2 2026 quarterly data extends the net-interest-margin compression documented in fy2025_recovery_driven_by_investment_income_not_lending_margin into outright negative territory: discrete net interest income was still marginally positive in Q1 2026 (137.17m) but swung NEGATIVE in Q2 2026 alone (-99.31m, interest paid of 3,420.16m exceeded interest income of 3,320.85m) -- the first quarter this dataset has recorded for NRBC where interest expense outright exceeds interest income. Cumulative H1 2026 net interest income was just 37.86m, down from 1,751.00m in the comparable H1 2025 period per this filing's own comparative column (-97.8%). As in FY2024-2025, the bank remained profitable only because investment income kept growing (1,761.93m in Q1 alone, 3,693.16m cumulative through H1) -- discrete Q2 2026 profit after tax was still a positive 361.02m despite the negative net interest income.

insights.historical_context: NRB Commercial Bank opened in April 2013 and this thirteen-year series is its entire public history. For eleven of those years it looked like a fast-growing fourth-generation success: total assets compounded at 33.6% a year from 9,538m to 217,993m by FY2023, a 23-fold increase and the fastest growth of any bank in this dataset, with a classified-loan ratio that never exceeded 5.35% and profit after tax rising from 22m to a 2,084m peak in FY2021. FY2024 broke that completely. Classified loans nearly tripled to 22,837m (15.47% of the book) while the book itself grew only 1.7%; profit after tax fell 98.1% to 36m; net interest income fell 95% to 187m as funding costs rose 43.3%; stockholder equity fell for the first time ever; and the bank moved from a 1,753.72m capital surplus to a 754.81m shortfall, with the Tier-I ratio at 7.64%. Provision coverage of classified loans halved to 22.1%, leaving 17,794m unprovided against 13,297m of equity. This is the same FY2024 recognition event visible at IFIC, Islami Bank and National Bank, and NRBC's position sits between the extremes: far worse than Midland Bank's 3.78%, far better than IFIC's 54.97%, and — unlike Islami Bank — it did let the loss show in the reported profit rather than holding it back through provisioning. FY2025 did not mark a turnaround so much as a partial, uneven stabilisation: profit after tax recovered to 330m (still 81-84% below the FY2021-2023 range) while the loan book resumed growing (+10.1%) and deposits grew again (+8.3%), but classified loans grew even faster (+22.1%) so the NPL ratio kept climbing to a new high of 17.17%, and the capital position kept eroding — CRAR fell to 11.15% and the capital shortfall widened 2.9x to 2,183m. Five straight years of rising NPL (2.93% at FY2020 to 17.17% at FY2025, every year higher than the last) and CRAR falling in two of the last three years (13.70% at FY2023 to 11.15% at FY2025), running through the one year profit nominally recovered, is the headline finding of the FY2025 update.
insights.data_gaps: This series runs FY2013-FY2025, thirteen years. FY2011 and FY2012 are not applicable — the bank opened in April 2013. Q1-Q3 interim data was added in a later session for FY2014-2019 (income-statement only, discrete quarters, from each year's own annual report -- no balance-sheet snapshot exists for these interim dates) and FY2020-2025 (full balance sheet + income statement, from the bank's own real interim filings at nrbcommercialbank.com/about/reports, solo basis except FY2021 Q2-Q3 which are consolidated-only -- see quarterly/2021_Q2.json and 2021_Q3.json). FY2013 (the bank's part-year opening year) remains without interim data; FY2026 Q1-Q2 were extracted in a later session (2026-09-12, solo basis, same font-corruption-requiring-visual-read pattern as FY2023-2025) and Q3 2026 is not yet due. See sources.json for the specific gaps within the covered years (illegible off-balance-sheet or NAV cells in a handful of font-corrupted or OCR-corrupted source filings). There is a BASIS BREAK at FY2020: FY2013-FY2019 are consolidated and FY2020-FY2025 solo (0.12% difference at the one year where both are measurable, and FY2025 is explicitly labelled 'Solo' in its own source table). Five of the thirteen years are not sourced from their own report, because those reports are absent from the archive or extract with no usable table. Three extraction traps were resolved before sourcing and are documented in full in sources.json: the FY2020 and FY2022 reports print FY2016-FY2018 total assets INCLUDING off-balance-sheet items (roughly 29% too high, proved exactly); the FY2021 report's only extractable table is a percentage-based horizontal analysis; and the FY2025 report is an image-only PDF with no text layer at all, requiring every figure to be read directly off the rendered table image rather than parsed as text (all cross-checked against the existing FY2024 record and internally against RWA-based ratios). That FY2025 cross-check surfaced two genuine discrepancies against the existing FY2024 record — Deposit (183,282m vs 169,737m) and Profit after tax (35.88m, which does not reconcile with that report's own PBT-tax, vs 44.77m, which does) — both left as documented divergences per standing methodology rather than edited into the existing FY2024 file; and one internal inconsistency inside the FY2025 report's own table, where printed Tier I + Tier II (18,870m) does not equal the same table's printed Regulatory Capital total (18,084m), which independently reconciles with the printed CRAR and capital-surplus rows instead. Reported return-on-assets and return-on-equity rows were captured for the first time in FY2025 (2.45% / 0.13%, average-balance basis per the bank's own table); ratios_timeseries.json also carries period-end recomputations for comparability with earlier years, which have none. EPS and NAV per share are likewise available for FY2025 only (0.398 and 16.48 respectively) — every earlier year's source tables carried no per-share or market-price figures at all, so P/E and price-to-book remain absent throughout, including FY2025 (a P/E of 12.56 is reported but a precise implied market price was not back-derived given rounding in both PE and EPS).

sources.notes: NRB Commercial Bank opened in April 2013, so this 13-year series (FY2013-FY2025) is the bank's entire public history and FY2011/FY2012 are not applicable. Two extraction traps had to be resolved before any figure could be trusted, both settled arithmetically rather than by assumption. FIRST, the off-balance-sheet trap: the FY2022 report's summary table prints FY2018 total assets as 86,598.12, which is exactly that year's balance-sheet total (67,142.86) plus its off-balance-sheet items (19,455.25); the same holds for FY2017 (57,529.35 + 16,591.43 = 74,120.78) and FY2016 (53,619.10 + 12,934.95 = 66,554.05) in the FY2020 report's balance-sheet-analysis table. SECOND, the FY2021 report is excluded entirely: its only extractable table is a horizontal analysis in which every value is a percentage of a base year, so a naive parse returns 100 for total assets in every year. These are recorded in detail because both would have put a silent ~29% step change into the middle of the series. THIRD (FY2025): the FY2025 annual report PDF is entirely image-based (0 lines from pdftotext -layout; native page images are only 845x1233px/72ppi) and its live-linked download host (sbplc.nrbcommercialbank.com) refuses or times out every connection attempt from every network path tried, including a third-party fetch service — the file was instead retrieved from the bank's older, still-live asset path (see sources list below) and all figures were read directly off the rendered table image rather than via pdftotext.

sources.note: The FY2013 and FY2014 reports extract with no usable table, so those years are this report's comparative columns. FY2013 is a part-year (the bank opened in April 2013) and is recorded with nil classified loans: no classified-loan figure is printed for FY2013 or FY2014 and the first appears in FY2015 at 0.27%.

There is no FY2016 report in the archive, so FY2016 comes from the FY2017 report. The FY2017 report's table covers FY2013-FY2016 only and does not carry its own year, so FY2017 comes from the FY2018 report. These three years are exactly the ones the later reports inflate with off-balance-sheet items, which is why they are sourced here and never from FY2020-FY2022.

Each year from its own report. The basis break sits here: the FY2019 table reports FY2019 total assets as 90,227.26 (consolidated) while the FY2020 report's 'Five Years' Key Performance Indicators' table reports 90,118.08 for the same year, which matches the FY2019 report's own SOLO balance sheet exactly. FY2019 is recorded on the consolidated basis from its own report; FY2020 onward is solo.

The FY2021 report carries no usable table (see notes), so FY2021 comes from this report. Its FY2018 column is excluded from sourcing because it is off-balance-sheet-inflated; its FY2019 onward columns are clean.
The FY2023 report's summary table does not extract usable balance-sheet rows, so FY2023 comes from this report. FY2024 is contemporaneous.

Total liabilities are total assets minus stockholder equity. Net interest income, where not printed, is interest income minus interest expense. Where the source report does not print total regulatory capital, it is derived as that same report's Tier-I plus Tier-II rather than borrowed from a later report, so the capital stack stays internally consistent — using the later report's total instead left a 0.7-0.8% gap at FY2018 and FY2019. Where CRAR is not printed it is derived as total capital over risk-weighted assets. sources.note: NEW EXTRACTION TRAP found this session, distinct from a plain OCR-of-a-scan corruption: these six PDFs have a genuine digital text layer (real embedded CID/TrueType fonts, not scanned images) but the fonts' glyph-to-Unicode mapping is broken for SOME glyphs -- e.g. the digit '1' silently extracts as the letter 'L' in some cells (e.g. '9,L89,498,L75') while other digits in the very same cell, and '1's in other cells of the same document, extract correctly. This is NOT a fixed substitution cipher (ruled out: tried plain pdftotext, pdftotext -raw, and mutool draw -F text, all reproduce the same corruption; a global 'L means 1' find-and-replace would corrupt the many cells where 'L'/'l' legitimately extract fine), so it cannot be reversed programmatically with confidence. All affected Balance Sheets and Profit and Loss Accounts were instead read directly off the rendered page images (175dpi) -- same methodology as this dataset's FY2025 annual report. Severity varies file to file (an automated scan for the corruption pattern counted roughly 38-136 affected digit-groups per file, heaviest in the FY2025 filings); off-balance-sheet exposures were legible in some of these visually-read pages (2023 Q1, 2025 Q1, 2025 Q3) but not others (2024 Q2, 2024 Q3, 2025 Q2), recorded as a per-file gap rather than guessed where illegible. Worth flagging in the shared parser/trap notes for other banks in this dataset, since it will recur wherever a bank's report was produced by whatever tool generated these ones' broken ToUnicode CMaps.
